Ketchup was once sold in pharmacies, as medicine.
The first ketchups weren't even made from tomatoes. They were made from mushrooms, walnuts, even fish.
Then in 1834, an American doctor named John Cook Bennett claimed tomatoes could cure diarrhea and indigestion.
He published recipes for tomato ketchup, and people believed him.
Soon, salesmen were selling tomato pills, promising cures for almost anything.
But the pills barely had any tomato in them, and the craze collapsed by the 1850s.
Ketchup survived anyway. Just in the kitchen, not the pharmacy.
